Aria (PM): kicking off PRD review for the Dedicated Capacity commitment product. TL;DR — customers want predictable throughput with firm commit tiers, a clear SLA for latency & availability, and safe autoscale behavior. Need scope + acceptance criteria by Thu EOD.
Kofi (Eng): +1. I sketched throughput buckets (small/med/large) and a baseline qps -> GPU mapping. Will share numbers.
Maya (SRE): We need to call out cold-start/KV-cache warmup effects in acceptance criteria. Without warm cache p95 will spike.
Priya (SE): Customer asks: guaranteed regional isolation (EU-only) and option to pin model family. Also wants explicit fallback model documented.
Liam (Sales): Two pilot customers pushing for 100% commit on a weeknight window. They want SLA credits for misses, but flexible overage pricing. We should define how overage is billed.
Aria (PM): Draft acceptance list I want feedback on: 1) Throughput sizing: baseline commit handles N sustained QPS for 99.9% of 30d windows; 2) Latency SLO: P95 <= 250ms for text-gen at typical seq len 256; 3) Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly; 4) Autoscale: spin-up < 30s and bounded by commit vs burst policy; 5) Fallbacks: automatic reroute to compatible model within 5s if primary unavailable; 6) Billing: overage rate caps.
Kofi (Eng): For (2) we should split by model class. 250ms is reasonable for quantized Llama-2 13B, not for unquantized 70B. Suggest specify per-model-class targets.
Maya (SRE): For autoscale timing, 30s is optimistic for cold GPU spin-up. If we rely on warm pool, we can hit 15s. Let's define two modes: warm-pool (target 15s) vs cold-provision (target 120s) and document fallbacks.
Priya (SE): Edge case: long prompts + streaming clients — if prefix cache is large, latency will exceed SLO. Acceptance criteria should include guidance: we only guarantee SLO for inputs <= 2k tokens; longer inputs are best-effort.
Liam (Sales): Contract negotiation point: customers want both committed baseline and burst to 3x for 1 hour/day. Propose we include 'burst credits' bucket sold as add-on.
Eva (CTO): Need to call out perf regression gate: no release to prod for dedicated unless perf regression vs benchmark <5% across our perf harness. Also legal needs explicit wording for SLA credits and force majeure.
Aria (PM): Good. I'll update PRD: add per-model-class SLO table, warm vs cold autoscale modes, input-size guidance, and billing model (committed + burst credits + overage). Will paste a short autoscale policy snippet for review.
Aria (PM): ```autoscale_policy:
  baseline_qps: 100
  burst_multiplier: 3
  burst_window_seconds: 3600
  warm_pool_size: 2  # number of prewarmed nodes
  cold_provision_timeout_seconds: 120
```
Kofi (Eng): That looks sane. Question: warm_pool_size=2 may not be enough for per-node GPU memory constraints. We should express warm pool in vGPUs or capacity units.
Maya (SRE): Also add metrics & alerting acceptance: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, 1-min burn rate alerts, and a playbook for failover to hosted pool.
Priya (SE): For customer-facing docs: include explicit sequence of steps for model fallback, and a test harness customers can run to validate commit. Customers will want deterministic testcases.
Liam (Sales): I'll flag that customers insist on a 30-day notice for rolling upgrades that might impact latency. Add to launch criteria.
Aria (PM): Launch criteria draft: 1) Perf bench green across model classes; 2) Monitoring dashboards live + alerting; 3) Billing flows tested (commits, burst, overage); 4) Legal sign-off on SLA wording; 5) At least one pilot customer onboarded and smoke-tested in region.
Eva (CTO): Ops ownership: infra team owns warm pool and autoscale runtime; SRE owns SLO dashboards & playbooks; PM owns billing acceptance. Make owners explicit in PRD.
Kofi (Eng): Open engineering risks: kernel selection for quantized 4-bit path, upstream lib compatibility, and cross-region routing edge cases. I'll add mitigation notes.
Maya (SRE): Edge-case list to include: inter-region network partitions, KV-cache corruption on failover, and partial node failures while autoscale in progress. Define deterministic behavior for each.
Aria (PM): OK folks — ask: review PRD draft I just pushed (link) and drop comments inline. Callouts I need decisions on by Thu: (A) per-model-class SLO table numbers, (B) burst credits pricing model, (C) warm_pool sizing semantics.
Priya (SE): I'll run pilot validation checklist with customer this week and report back.
Liam (Sales): I'll push the proposed pricing for burst credits to legal and finance.
Kofi (Eng): I'll follow up with a short sizing spreadsheet mapping qps->gpus and share by EOD tomorrow.
Maya (SRE): I'll add the playbook and alert runbooks; will need a small runbook review session.
DeployBot: deploy/ci update: perf-harness job completed successfully on staging (tags: dedicated-prd/bench-2025-07-03) :white_check_mark:
Aria (PM): Thanks — will collect final signoffs after comments. If anyone has strong objections to the acceptance criteria above, please call them out here. :pray:
